headline: Rock Legend Slash Honored With New Snake Species Named After Him
meta_description: Scientists discovered a new nonvenomous snake in New Guinea and named it after Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, who has supported wildlife conservation since chi…
summary_short: A newly identified reddish-brown groundsnake from New Guinea has been formally named Lielaphis slashi after the legendary guitarist—honoring his lifelong passion for rep…
body:
When field researchers first spotted an unfamiliar reddish-brown snake in New Guinea's forests, they had no idea it would eventually bear the name of one of rock music's most recognizable figures. Scientists have now formally identified the 28-inch-long creature as a previously unknown species and named it Lielaphis slashi—Slash's groundsnake—after Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, whose genuine love for reptiles since childhood made him an ideal namesake. The nonvenomous snake was discovered during fieldwork in 2006, but genetic testing and physical analysis only recently confirmed it as a distinct species, with differences in scale counts and genetic markers setting it apart from related snakes in the same genus.

The honor carries real personal meaning. Sara Ruane, the Field Museum's Associate Curator of Herpetology who led the research, has long admired Slash. She recalled seeing him on the cover of Reptiles Magazine in fifth grade, holding a reticulated python, which sparked her own journey toward studying herpetology. Years later, when Ruane had the opportunity to name newly recognized species, she returned to that old interview and discovered Slash's genuine passion for museums, zoos, and childhood snake hunts. "This guy is so cool," she thought—and decided he deserved this unusual honor.

Though scientists still know relatively little about the snake's behavior, its anatomy offers clues. The large teeth at the back of its mouth likely help it grasp small, slippery-scaled lizards and reptile eggs. Despite its rock-and-roll name, L. slashi poses no threat to humans. However, the forests of New Guinea where it lives face real danger from coffee farming and mining operations, making the identification and protection of such species increasingly urgent.
quick_facts: New snake species discovered in New Guinea's tropical forests in 2006
Named Lielaphis slashi after Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash
Measures 28 inches long, reddish-brown, entirely nonvenomous
Distinguished by genetic analysis and differences in scale counts
Identified through research at Field Museum and Louisiana State University
